$comment: Task recipes + search synonyms for the MCP server. Single source of truth: loaded by src/server.ts (TS), mirrored to rust/recipes.json for the Rust crate, and exported to skills/<id>/SKILL.md by scripts/build-skills.mjs. VERIFICATION STATUS: every operation name and the request-body fields quoted here are checked against tools.json (scripts/build-skills.mjs fails the build on unknown names); the step ORDER and state rules follow Apple's documented API behaviour and have NOT been executed against a live App Store Connect account - confirm against Apple's docs when a step returns 409/403.

recipes.title: Submit an app version for App Review
recipes.description: Use when the user wants to submit, send, or hand off a version to Apple App Review (submit for review, send to review, add to review, ready for review). Chains app -> appStoreVersion -> reviewSubmission -> reviewSubmissionItem -> submitted.

args.name: app_id
args.description: App resource id (numeric). Find via apps_getCollection filter[bundleId] if unknown.

steps: 1. Pick the version to submit: `apps_appStoreVersions_getToManyRelated` with path id={{app_id}}, query `filter[platform]`={{platform}} and `fields[appStoreVersions]=versionString,appStoreState,build`. Candidate states that can be submitted: PREORDER_READY_FOR_REVIEW, READY_FOR_REVIEW, REPLACED_WITH_NEW_DEVELOPER_REJECTED_VERSION, DEVELOPER_REJECTED, REJECTED (after fixing metadata). Record `versionId` = data[0].id.

2. Reuse an open submission if one exists: `reviewSubmissions_getCollection` with `filter[platform]`={{platform}} and `filter[app]`={{app_id}}. A submission with attributes.state READY_FOR_REVIEW or UNRESOLVED_ISSUES can take more items; otherwise create a new one in step 3.

3. Create the submission (if needed): `reviewSubmissions_createInstance` with `_body` = { data: { type: 'reviewSubmissions', attributes: { platform: {{platform}} }, relationships: { app: { data: { type: 'apps', id: '{{app_id}}' } } } } }. Record `submissionId` = data.id.

4. Attach the version: `reviewSubmissionItems_createInstance` with `_body` = { data: { type: 'reviewSubmissionItems', relationships: { reviewSubmission: { data: { type: 'reviewSubmissions', id: submissionId } }, appStoreVersion: { data: { type: 'appStoreVersions', id: versionId } } } } }.

5. Submit: `reviewSubmissions_updateInstance` with path id=submissionId and `_body` = { data: { type: 'reviewSubmissions', id: submissionId, attributes: { submitted: true } } }. Confirm data.attributes.state becomes WAITING_FOR_REVIEW.
6. Report: version string, submission state, and any items with state UNRESOLVED_ISSUES (these block submission until fixed).
pitfalls: Only one review submission per platform can be open at a time; always check step 2 before creating.
Items can only be added while the submission is READY_FOR_REVIEW or UNRESOLVED_ISSUES.
The version must have a build attached and all required metadata; if appStoreState is not submittable, fix metadata first (see update-store-listing) or attach a build (see replace-build-on-version).
Platform attribute must match the version's platform; MAC_OS vs IOS mismatch is rejected.

recipes.title: Configure release type, schedule, phased release, or release now
recipes.description: Use when the user asks about manual release, automatic release, scheduled release, phased release, release after approval, or releasing an approved version now.

args.name: version_id
args.description: appStoreVersion resource id (or resolve from app_id via apps_appStoreVersions_getToManyRelated).

steps: 1. Read current settings: `appStoreVersions_getInstance` with path id={{version_id}} and `fields[appStoreVersions]=versionString,appStoreState,releaseType,earliestReleaseDate`. Also `appStoreVersions_appStoreVersionPhasedRelease_getToOneRelated` to see if a phased release exists.

2. Set the release type: `appStoreVersions_updateInstance` with path id={{version_id}} and `_body` = { data: { type: 'appStoreVersions', id: '{{version_id}}', attributes: { releaseType: 'MANUAL' | 'AFTER_APPROVAL' | 'SCHEDULED' } } }. For SCHEDULED also set `earliestReleaseDate` (ISO 8601 with time, in the past is rejected).

3. Phased release (optional, after approval only): if none exists, `appStoreVersionPhasedReleases_createInstance` with `_body` = { data: { type: 'appStoreVersionPhasedReleases', attributes: { phasedReleaseState: 'ACTIVE' }, relationships: { appStoreVersion: { data: { type: 'appStoreVersions', id: '{{version_id}}' } } } } }. Later control with `appStoreVersionPhasedReleases_updateInstance`: phasedReleaseState ACTIVE | PAUSED | COMPLETE.

4. Release a MANUAL version now (only when appStoreState is PENDING_DEVELOPER_RELEASE): `appStoreVersionReleaseRequests_createInstance` with `_body` = { data: { type: 'appStoreVersionReleaseRequests', relationships: { appStoreVersion: { data: { type: 'appStoreVersions', id: '{{version_id}}' } } } } }.
5. Verify with `appStoreVersions_getInstance` and report releaseType, earliestReleaseDate, phasedRelease state and appStoreState.
pitfalls: PENDING_DEVELOPER_RELEASE means approved and waiting for the developer - that is when step 4 applies, not before.
Phased release must be enabled before the version is approved; it cannot be started retroactively.
Changing releaseType is a PATCH of attributes only - never send relationships unless you intend to change the build.

recipes.title: Replace the build attached to a version
recipes.description: Use when the user wants to swap, replace, attach, or change the build of an app store version (e.g. after rejection, or to attach a newer build before submission).

args.name: build_id
args.description: Processed build id (optional; if omitted, list the latest valid builds so the user can choose).

steps: 1. Find candidate builds: `builds_getCollection` with query `filter[app]` (app id from the version), `filter[preReleaseVersion.version]`=<versionString> (must equal the version's versionString), `filter[processingState]`=VALID, `sort`=-uploadedDate, `limit`=10, `fields[builds]=version,uploadedDate,expired,processingState`. Pick `buildId`.

2. Attach: `appStoreVersions_updateInstance` with path id={{version_id}} and `_body` = { data: { type: 'appStoreVersions', id: '{{version_id}}', relationships: { build: { data: { type: 'builds', id: buildId } } } } }.
3. Verify with `builds_appStoreVersion_getToOneRelated` (path id=buildId) or `appStoreVersions_getInstance` with include=build.
pitfalls: Only allowed while the version is in PREORDER_READY_FOR_REVIEW, READY_FOR_REVIEW, DEVELOPER_REJECTED, REPLACED_WITH_NEW_DEVELOPER_REJECTED_VERSION, REJECTED, or INVALID_BINARY; also triggered automatically when a build expires.
The build's preReleaseVersion.version must match the versionString; a build uploaded with a different CFBundleShortVersionString is invisible to this filter.
If the version is WAITING_FOR_REVIEW it cannot be changed - it must be withdrawn first.

recipes.title: Find the latest processed build for an app
recipes.description: Use when the user asks for the newest/latest build, build list, build status, processing state, or which builds exist for a version.
steps: 1. `builds_getCollection` with query `filter[app]`={{app_id}}, `sort`=-uploadedDate, `limit`=20, `fields[builds]=version,uploadedDate,processingState,expired,buildNumber,cfBundleVersion`, and include=preReleaseVersion. Add `filter[preReleaseVersion.version]`={{version}} if given, and `filter[processingState]`=VALID to hide failed builds.
2. Read data[0] as the newest. Report uploadedDate, processingState (VALID | PROCESSING | FAILED | INVALID), expired flag, and the id for chaining.
3. For TestFlight state add `builds_betaAppReviewSubmission_getToOneRelated` (path id=buildId) to see betaReviewState.
pitfalls: processingState=VALID means ready; PROCESSING builds cannot be attached or distributed yet.
expired=true builds cannot be submitted; the version then needs a replacement build (see replace-build-on-version).

recipes.title: Distribute a build to testers via TestFlight
recipes.description: Use when the user wants to distribute, push, or share a build with testers, create or manage beta groups, enable public link, or submit a build for external TestFlight beta review.

args.name: external
args.description: true for external testers (requires beta review); false/omitted for internal group (App Store Connect users only, up to 100).

steps: 1. Find or create the group: `betaGroups_getCollection` with `filter[app]`={{app_id}}, `filter[name]`=<group name>. If missing, `betaGroups_createInstance` with `_body` = { data: { type: 'betaGroups', attributes: { name, isInternalGroup: !external, hasAccessToAllBuilds: false, publicLinkEnabled: false, feedbackEnabled: true }, relationships: { app: { data: { type: 'apps', id: '{{app_id}}' } } } } }. Record `groupId`.
2. Attach the build: `betaGroups_builds_createToManyRelationship` with path id=groupId and `_body` = { data: [{ type: 'builds', id: '{{build_id}}' }] }.

3. External only - export compliance: `builds_appEncryptionDeclaration_getToOneRelated` (path id={{build_id}}) to see if the build already has a declaration; otherwise `apps_appEncryptionDeclarations_getToManyRelated` (path id={{app_id}}) to find a reusable one. Create with `appEncryptionDeclarations_createInstance`: attributes { containsProprietaryCryptography: true, containsThirdPartyCryptography: false, availableOnFrenchStore: true, appDescription }, relationships.app. Then attach it to the build: `builds_appEncryptionDeclaration_updateToOneRelationship` with `_body` = { data: { type: 'appEncryptionDeclarations', id } }.

4. External only - beta review: `betaAppReviewSubmissions_createInstance` with `_body` = { data: { type: 'betaAppReviewSubmissions', relationships: { build: { data: { type: 'builds', id: '{{build_id}}' } } } } }. Poll `builds_betaAppReviewSubmission_getToOneRelated` until attributes.betaReviewState is APPROVED (usually minutes to a day). Internal groups skip this.

5. Add testers: see manage-beta-testers. Enable a public link with `betaGroups_updateInstance` attributes { publicLinkEnabled: true, publicLinkLimitEnabled, publicLinkLimit }; the link itself (attributes.publicLink) is read-only and appears on the group after enabling.
6. Verify: `betaGroups_builds_getToManyRelated` and `betaGroups_getInstance`.
pitfalls: Internal groups: testers must already be App Store Connect users with access to the app. External groups: testers can be any email, but the build must pass beta review once per version.
Beta review is required for the first build of each version; later builds of the same version usually do not need another review.
Export compliance must be resolved before external distribution; missing declarations block review.

recipes.title: Add or remove TestFlight beta testers
recipes.description: Use when the user wants to add, invite, remove, list, or import beta testers, or manage tester membership in a beta group.
steps: 1. Check existing testers: `betaTesters_getCollection` with `filter[email]`=<email>, `filter[app]`=<app id>. Record testerId if present.

2. New tester + group in one call: `betaTesters_createInstance` with `_body` = { data: { type: 'betaTesters', attributes: { email, firstName, lastName }, relationships: { betaGroups: { data: [{ type: 'betaGroups', id: '{{group_id}}' }] } } } }.
3. Existing tester into the group: `betaGroups_betaTesters_createToManyRelationship` with path id={{group_id}} and `_body` = { data: [{ type: 'betaTesters', id: testerId }] }.
4. Limit which builds a tester sees: `betaTesters_builds_createToManyRelationship` (path id=testerId) with builds; otherwise they get all builds the group has.
5. Remove: `betaTesters_betaGroups_deleteToManyRelationship` or `betaTesters_deleteInstance`. List: `betaGroups_betaTesters_getToManyRelated` (path id={{group_id}}).
pitfalls: Tester emails are Apple IDs; duplicates across groups of the same app are the same betaTester resource - link, do not recreate.
Deleting a betaTester removes them from all groups of the app.

recipes.title: Update App Store listing metadata (description, keywords, what's new, URLs)
recipes.description: Use when the user wants to edit, update, or set app store description, keywords, promotional text, what's new text, support/marketing URL, screenshots ordering text, or localize the product page.

args.name: locale
args.description: Locale tag, e.g. en-US, zh-Hans. Defaults to the app's primaryLocale.

steps: 1. Get localizations: `appStoreVersions_appStoreVersionLocalizations_getToManyRelated` with path id={{version_id}}, `filter[locale]`={{locale}} (optional). Record `localizationId` and the app's primaryLocale from `apps_getInstance` if needed.

2. If the locale is missing: `appStoreVersionLocalizations_createInstance` with `_body` = { data: { type: 'appStoreVersionLocalizations', attributes: { locale }, relationships: { appStoreVersion: { data: { type: 'appStoreVersions', id: '{{version_id}}' } } } } }.

3. Edit: `appStoreVersionLocalizations_updateInstance` with path id=localizationId and only the attributes to change: description, keywords (comma separated, <=100 characters), promotionalText (<=170), marketingUrl, supportUrl, whatsNew (required for updates), and for the primary locale the keywords are the ones that matter for search.
4. Verify with `appStoreVersionLocalizations_getInstance`.
pitfalls: PATCH only the attributes you change; sending empty strings clears fields.
whatsNew is required for every new version except the first; missing it leaves the version not submittable.
Keywords are shared across locales? No - each locale has its own; the primary locale carries the most weight.

recipes.title: Manage App Store screenshots and previews
recipes.description: Use when the user wants to upload, add, reorder, replace, or delete App Store screenshots or app previews (videos) for a version.
steps: 1. List sets: `appStoreVersionLocalizations_appScreenshotSets_getToManyRelated` with path id={{localization_id}}, include=appScreenshots. Each set has a screenshotDisplayType (e.g. APP_IPHONE_67, APP_IPAD_PRO_3GEN_129).

2. Create a set if needed: `appScreenshotSets_createInstance` with `_body` = { data: { type: 'appScreenshotSets', attributes: { screenshotDisplayType }, relationships: { appStoreVersionLocalization: { data: { type: 'appStoreVersionLocalizations', id: '{{localization_id}}' } } } } }. Record `setId`.

3. Reserve the image: `appScreenshots_createInstance` with `_body` = { data: { type: 'appScreenshots', attributes: { fileName, fileSize }, relationships: { appScreenshotSet: { data: { type: 'appScreenshotSets', id: setId } } } } }. The response has `uploadOperations` (method, url, length, offset, requestHeaders) - upload the bytes to those URLs (this MCP cannot transfer binary; do it with curl/HTTP from the client) and compute the checksum.

4. Commit: `appScreenshots_updateInstance` with path id=<screenshot id> and `_body` = { data: { type: 'appScreenshots', id, attributes: { uploaded: true, sourceFileChecksum } } }. Poll `appScreenshots_getInstance` until assetDeliveryState.state is COMPLETE.

5. Reorder: `appScreenshotSets_appScreenshots_replaceToManyRelationship` with path id=setId and `_body` = { data: [{ type: 'appScreenshots', id }, ...] } in the desired order. Delete with `appScreenshots_deleteInstance`.

6. Videos: same flow with appPreviewSets / appPreviews - `appPreviewSets_createInstance` (attributes previewType), `appPreviews_createInstance` (attributes fileName, fileSize, mimeType, previewFrameTimeCode; relationships.appPreviewSet).
pitfalls: A set needs 1-10 screenshots (some display types require at least 3) before the version can be submitted.
Checksum format and size limits per display type are in get_tool_details(appScreenshots_updateInstance) - verify there before committing.
Until uploaded=true the reservation expires; re-reserve if the upload did not finish.

recipes.title: Create an auto-renewable subscription with pricing and submit it
recipes.description: Use when the user wants to create, add, or set up an auto-renewable subscription, subscription group, subscription price, introductory offer, or submit a subscription for review.
steps: 1. Group: `apps_subscriptionGroups_getToManyRelated` with path id={{app_id}} (filter[name] if you know the reference name); create if missing with `subscriptionGroups_createInstance` (_body attributes { referenceName }, relationships.app). Record `groupId`.

2. Subscription: `subscriptions_createInstance` with `_body` = { data: { type: 'subscriptions', attributes: { name, productId, subscriptionPeriod: 'ONE_MONTH' | 'ONE_WEEK' | 'ONE_YEAR' | ..., familySharable: false, groupLevel: 1 }, relationships: { group: { data: { type: 'subscriptionGroups', id: groupId } } } } }. Record `subscriptionId`. productId is immutable.
3. Localization: `subscriptionLocalizations_createInstance` with attributes { name, locale, description } and relationships.subscription. One per locale.

4. Price point: `subscriptions_pricePoints_getToManyRelated` with path id=subscriptionId and `filter[territory]`=USA (territory ids are ISO codes from `territories_getCollection`). Pick customerPrice, record `pricePointId`.

5. Price: `subscriptionPrices_createInstance` with `_body` = { data: { type: 'subscriptionPrices', attributes: { startDate: null, preserveCurrentPrice: false }, relationships: { subscription: {...}, territory: { data: { type: 'territories', id: 'USA' } }, subscriptionPricePoint: { data: { type: 'subscriptionPricePoints', id: pricePointId } } } } }.

6. Review screenshot (required for first submission): `subscriptionAppStoreReviewScreenshots_createInstance` with attributes { fileName, fileSize } and relationships.subscription; upload bytes, then `subscriptionAppStoreReviewScreenshots_updateInstance` with uploaded=true.

7. Submit: `subscriptionSubmissions_createInstance` with relationships.subscription. Then poll `subscriptions_getInstance` (path id=subscriptionId) and read attributes.state until APPROVED (or REJECTED - inspect the submission items).
8. Optional introductory offer: `subscriptionIntroductoryOffers_createInstance` (relationships subscription + territory + subscriptionPricePoint, attributes duration, numberOfPeriods, offerMode).
pitfalls: The subscription must be in state MISSING_METADATA until localization, price and screenshot exist; only then submit.
Only one submission can be in flight at a time; a rejected submission needs the items fixed and a new submission.
productId and subscriptionPeriod cannot be changed after creation.

recipes.title: Create, localize, price, and submit an in-app purchase (IAP v2)
recipes.description: Use when the user wants to create, add, set up, localize, price, or submit an in-app purchase / consumable / non-consumable / non-renewing subscription (IAP v2).

args.name: app_id
args.description: App resource id the IAP belongs to.

args.name: iap_id
args.description: Existing inAppPurchases (v2) resource id when localizing/pricing/submitting an existing product; omit to create a new one.

steps: 1. Create (skip if iap_id is known): `inAppPurchasesV2_createInstance` (POST /v2/inAppPurchases) with `_body` = { data: { type: 'inAppPurchases', attributes: { name, productId, inAppPurchaseType: 'CONSUMABLE' | 'NON_CONSUMABLE' | 'NON_RENEWING_SUBSCRIPTION', familySharable: false, reviewNote }, relationships: { app: { data: { type: 'apps', id: '{{app_id}}' } } } } }. Record `iapId` = data.id. productId is immutable.

2. Inspect: `inAppPurchasesV2_getInstance` (path id={{iap_id}}); localizations via `inAppPurchasesV2_inAppPurchaseLocalizations_getToManyRelated`; state is in attributes.state (MISSING_METADATA until steps 3-4 are done).

3. Localization: `inAppPurchaseLocalizations_createInstance` with `_body` = { data: { type: 'inAppPurchaseLocalizations', attributes: { name, locale, description }, relationships: { inAppPurchaseV2: { data: { type: 'inAppPurchases', id: iapId } } } } }. One per locale; update with `inAppPurchaseLocalizations_updateInstance`.

4. Price point: `inAppPurchasesV2_pricePoints_getToManyRelated` with path id={{iap_id}} and `filter[territory]`=USA (territory ids are ISO codes from `territories_getCollection`); pick customerPrice, record `inAppPurchasePriceId`.

5. Price: `inAppPurchasePriceSchedules_createInstance` with relationships { inAppPurchase: { data: { type: 'inAppPurchases', id: iapId } }, baseTerritory: { data: { type: 'territories', id: 'USA' } }, manualPrices: { data: [{ type: 'inAppPurchasePrices', id: inAppPurchasePriceId }] } }. Note this endpoint uses `inAppPurchase` (not `inAppPurchaseV2`).

6. Optional review image: `inAppPurchaseImages_createInstance` (attributes fileName, fileSize, relationships.inAppPurchaseV2), upload bytes, then `inAppPurchaseImages_updateInstance` with uploaded=true.

7. Submit: `inAppPurchaseSubmissions_createInstance` with relationships.inAppPurchaseV2 = iapId. Then re-read `inAppPurchasesV2_getInstance` and watch attributes.state until APPROVED (or REJECTED - inspect the submission items).
pitfalls: Relationship names differ per endpoint: create/get/localize/submit use `inAppPurchases` / `inAppPurchaseV2`; the price schedule uses `inAppPurchase` and its manualPrices are `inAppPurchasePrices` (ids from pricePoints). Copy them exactly from get_tool_details.
productId and inAppPurchaseType are immutable after creation.
A review screenshot per localization is required before the first submission for some IAP types.
Only one submission can be in flight at a time.

recipes.title: Change the app price or price schedule
recipes.description: Use when the user wants to change, set, schedule, or inspect the app's price (tier, price point, base territory, manual/automatic prices).
steps: 1. Current schedule: `apps_appPriceSchedule_getToOneRelated` with path id={{app_id}} and include=manualPrices,baseTerritory.
2. Choose base territory (e.g. USA) via `territories_getCollection`; territory ids are ISO codes.
3. Choose the price point: `apps_appPricePoints_getToManyRelated` with path id={{app_id}} and `filter[territory]`=USA; pick customerPrice, record `pricePointId`.

4. Create a new schedule (this is how price changes are applied): `appPriceSchedules_createInstance` with `_body` = { data: { type: 'appPriceSchedules', relationships: { app: { data: { type: 'apps', id: '{{app_id}}' } }, baseTerritory: { data: { type: 'territories', id: 'USA' } }, manualPrices: { data: [{ type: 'appPrices', id: pricePointId }] } } } }. Optional attributes.startDate schedules the change. (The spec names the relationship type `appPrices` while the ids come from appPricePoints; if Apple rejects the type, retry with `appPricePoints`.)
5. Verify: `appPriceSchedules_manualPrices_getToManyRelated` and `appPriceSchedules_automaticPrices_getToManyRelated` (other territories follow automatically).
pitfalls: There is no PATCH for manual prices; every change is a new appPriceSchedule.
A schedule with a future startDate stays pending until that date; confirm with `apps_appPriceSchedule_getToOneRelated`.

recipes.title: Create offer codes for subscriptions or in-app purchases
recipes.description: Use when the user wants to create promo codes, offer codes, custom codes, or win-back offers for a subscription or in-app purchase.
steps: 1. Subscription: `subscriptionOfferCodes_createInstance` with `_body` = { data: { type: 'subscriptionOfferCodes', attributes: { name, offerEligibility: 'ACTIVE' | 'ALL', customerEligibilities: ['NEW', 'EXISTING', 'WIN_BACK'], offerMode: 'FREE_TRIAL' | 'PAY_AS_YOU_GO' | 'PAY_UP_FRONT', duration: 'ONE_MONTH' | ..., numberOfPeriods, targetSubscriptionPlanType: 'AUTO_RENEWABLE' }, relationships: { subscription: { data: { type: 'subscriptions', id: '{{product_id}}' } }, prices: { data: [{ type: 'subscriptionPrices', id }] } } } }.
2. IAP: `inAppPurchaseOfferCodes_createInstance` with attributes { name, customerEligibilities } and relationships { inAppPurchase, prices }.

3. Custom (one-time) codes: `subscriptionOfferCodeCustomCodes_createInstance` (relationships offerCode, attributes customCode or numberOfCodes, expirationDate) or `inAppPurchaseOfferCodeCustomCodes_createInstance`.

4. Win-back offers for subscriptions: `winBackOffers_createInstance` (attributes referenceName, offerId, duration, offerMode, periodCount, customerEligibility..., relationships subscription + prices).
5. Verify: `subscriptions_offerCodes_getToManyRelated` (path id=subscription) or `inAppPurchases_offerCodes...`.
pitfalls: Offer code `prices` must reference subscriptionPrices / inAppPurchasePrices already created for the product; create pricing first (see create-subscription / iap-localize-price-submit).
offerId and productId are immutable identifiers.

recipes.title: Read and reply to customer reviews
recipes.description: Use when the user wants to list, fetch, read, analyze, or respond to App Store customer reviews / ratings.
steps: 1. List: `apps_customerReviews_getToManyRelated` with path id={{app_id}}, query `sort`=-createdDate, `limit`=50, `filter[territory]` (optional ISO code), `filter[rating]` (optional), `fields[customerReviews]=rating,title,body,createdDate,territory`. Optional include=response to see existing replies.

2. Reply: `customerReviewResponses_createInstance` with `_body` = { data: { type: 'customerReviewResponses', attributes: { responseBody }, relationships: { review: { data: { type: 'customerReviews', id: reviewId } } } } }.
3. Replace a reply: `customerReviewResponses_deleteInstance` then create again (one response per review). Check state via `customerReviews_response_getToOneRelated` - PUBLISHED appears on the store.
pitfalls: Publishing is asynchronous; the response may stay PENDING for a while.
Apple allows one response per review; to change it, delete and recreate.

recipes.title: Download sales and finance reports
recipes.description: Use when the user wants sales reports, finance reports, revenue, earnings, downloads, or payment reports.
steps: 1. Sales: `salesReports_getCollection` with query `filter[frequency]`=DAILY | WEEKLY | MONTHLY | YEARLY, `filter[reportSubType]`=SUMMARY | DETAILED, `filter[reportType]`=SALES, `filter[vendorNumber]`=<vendor number from Payments and Financial Reports>, `filter[reportDate]`=YYYY-MM-DD (for DAILY) or YYYY-MM (MONTHLY) - call get_tool_details for the exact date formats. Returns data.attributes.url (a download link).

2. Finance: `financeReports_getCollection` with `filter[regionCode]` (e.g. US, CN, or ZZ for rest of world), `filter[reportType]`=FINANCIAL, `filter[vendorNumber]`, and the date filter per get_tool_details. Also returns a url.
3. Download the URL with a client-side HTTP request (this MCP returns the link; the file is not JSON).
pitfalls: Report dates use the report's own frequency granularity; DAILY takes a full date, MONTHLY takes YYYY-MM, YEARLY takes YYYY.
The vendorNumber is not the app id - find it in App Store Connect > Payments and Financial Reports.

recipes.title: Create signing certificate, register device, and provisioning profile
recipes.description: Use when the user wants to create a certificate, register a test device (UDID), or create a provisioning profile for development/ad-hoc/App Store distribution.

args.name: profile_type
args.description: IOS_APP_DEVELOPMENT | IOS_APP_STORE | IOS_APP_ADHOC | MAC_APP_DEVELOPMENT | MAC_APP_STORE | MAC_APP_DISTRIBUTION ... (full enum in get_tool_details profiles_createInstance).

steps: 1. Certificate: generate a CSR locally (openssl req -new -keyform PEM -keyout key.pem -out csr.pem -subj '/CN=Name/O=Org'), then `certificates_createInstance` with `_body` = { data: { type: 'certificates', attributes: { certificateType: 'IOS_DEVELOPMENT' | 'IOS_DISTRIBUTION' | 'MAC_APP_DEVELOPMENT' | 'MAC_APP_DISTRIBUTION' | ..., csrContent }, relationships: {} } }. The response contains certificateContent once - download and store it.
2. Device: `devices_createInstance` with attributes { name, platform: IOS | MAC_OS | TV_OS ..., udid }. List with `devices_getCollection`.

3. Profile: `profiles_createInstance` with `_body` = { data: { type: 'profiles', attributes: { name, profileType }, relationships: { bundleId: { data: { type: 'bundleIds', id } }, certificates: { data: [{ type: 'certificates', id }] }, devices: { data: [{ type: 'devices', id }] } } } }. devices is omitted for App Store profiles. Response includes profileContent (base64 .mobileprovision).
4. Inspect/download existing: `profiles_getCollection` (filter[name], filter[profileType]) and `profiles_getInstance`.
pitfalls: certificateContent and profileContent are returned only in the create/get responses; save them immediately.
Apple limits certificates per type; delete expired ones with certificates_deleteInstance first.
Bundle ids are registered with `bundleIds_createInstance` (attributes name, platform, identifier) if missing.

recipes.title: Invite users and manage App Store Connect team access
recipes.description: Use when the user wants to invite, add, or remove team members, change user roles, or control which apps a user can see.
steps: 1. List: `users_getCollection` with fields[users]=username,firstName,lastName,roles,allAppsVisible; pending invites via `userInvitations_getCollection`.

2. Invite: `userInvitations_createInstance` with `_body` = { data: { type: 'userInvitations', attributes: { email, firstName, lastName, roles: ['ADMIN' | 'FINANCE' | 'ACCOUNT_HOLDER' | 'SALES' | 'MARKETING' | 'APP_MANAGER' | 'DEVELOPER' | 'ACCESS_TO_REPORTS' | 'CUSTOMER_SUPPORT' | 'CREATE_APPS'], allAppsVisible: false }, relationships: { visibleApps: { data: [{ type: 'apps', id }] } } } }.

3. Change visible apps for an existing user: `users_visibleApps_replaceToManyRelationship` with path id=userId and `_body` = { data: [{ type: 'apps', id }, ...] }. Roles: `users_updateInstance` attributes.roles.
4. Remove: `users_deleteInstance` or `userInvitations_deleteInstance`.
pitfalls: ACCOUNT_HOLDER cannot be invited via API; the last ADMIN cannot be removed.
allAppsVisible=true ignores visibleApps.

recipes.title: Set age rating, app categories, and app info
recipes.description: Use when the user wants to set or change the age rating declaration, age rating override, primary/secondary categories, or app info localizations (subtitle, privacy policy URL, categories).
steps: 1. App info: `apps_appInfos_getToManyRelated` with path id={{app_id}}; record `appInfoId` and its appInfoLocalizations.

2. Age rating: `appInfos_ageRatingDeclaration_getToOneRelated` with path id=appInfoId, then `ageRatingDeclarations_updateInstance` with path id=<declaration id> and attributes (advertising, alcoholTobaccoOrDrugUseOrReferences, contests, gambling, gunsOrOtherWeapons, kidsAgeBand, lootBox, medicalOrTreatmentInformation, messagingAndChat, parentalControls, profanityOrCrudeHumor, sexualContentGraphicAndNudity, sexualContentOrNudity, horrorOrFearThemes, matureOrSuggestiveThemes, unrestrictedWebAccess, userGeneratedContent, violenceCartoonOrFantasy, violenceRealistic, violenceRealisticProlongedGraphicOrSadistic, ageRatingOverride, koreaAgeRatingOverride).

3. Categories: `appCategories_getCollection` to find ids, then `appInfos_updateInstance` with path id=appInfoId and relationships { primaryCategory, primarySubcategoryOne, primarySubcategoryTwo, secondaryCategory, ... } each as { data: { type: 'appCategories', id } }.

4. Subtitle / privacy policy URL / name per locale: `appInfoLocalizations_createInstance` (attributes locale, name, subtitle, privacyPolicyUrl, privacyChoicesUrl, privacyPolicyText; relationships.appInfo) or `appInfoLocalizations_updateInstance`.
pitfalls: Categories must be leaf categories (no children) and second category must differ from the first.
Age rating answers are required before the first submission of any version.

recipes.title: Set up App Store Connect webhooks (notifications)
recipes.description: Use when the user wants to create, test, or list App Store Connect server notifications / webhooks and their deliveries.

args.name: app_id
args.description: App resource id (or omit for all apps if the key allows).

steps: 1. List: `apps_webhooks_getToManyRelated` with path id={{app_id}} (use `webhooks_getInstance` only when you already have a webhook id).

2. Create: `webhooks_createInstance` with `_body` = { data: { type: 'webhooks', attributes: { name, url: 'https://...', enabled: true, eventTypes: ['APP_STORE_REVIEW_REQUESTED', 'TESTFLIGHT_BETA_TESTER_CONFIRMATION', ...] }, relationships: { app: { data: { type: 'apps', id: '{{app_id}}' } } } } }. Call get_tool_details for the full eventType enum.
3. Test: `webhookPings_createInstance` with relationships.webhook, then `webhooks_deliveries_getToManyRelated` (path id=webhookId) to inspect deliveryState SUCCEEDED | FAILED | PENDING and response.
4. Rotate secret: `webhooks_updateInstance` attributes.secret; verify signature header on your endpoint.
pitfalls: Endpoint must be HTTPS with a valid certificate and respond within 20 seconds.
A webhook can be attached to one app; create one per app for app-scoped events.
